days.title: Riverside and Ancient Settlements
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Poblado de la Loma de Betxí
stops.detail: Among them, Bronze Age sites (Poblado de la Loma de Betxí) stand out; the remains of a large Roman-era aqueduct; and from the Visigothic era (fortified settlement of Valencia la Vella) we can find Jurassic and Miocene formations, and a large architectural infrastructure (such as weirs, irrigation ditches, aqueducts, and reservoirs) used to harness the water of the Turia River for agricultural purposes.

stops.name: río Turia
stops.detail: The Turia-Guadalaviar River and its bank, of great ecological interest, Mediterranean pine and scrub forests and the Valencian orchard of medieval origin are representative environments of this natural area.

days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: la Vallesa
stops.detail: It will include three forested masses -la Vallesa, Les Rodanes and La Pea- and the banks of the Turia.

stops.name: Les Rodanes
stops.detail: The mountains of Les Rodanes and la Vallesa are the last hills (natural elevation of the land of low height) surrounded by plains, before reaching the plains near the mouth of the Turia River.

stops.name: La Pea
stops.detail: The steepest orography (or elevation) is found to the west of the Park in the mountains of Palmeral and La Pea.

stops.name: río Sot
stops.detail: This extension connects with the southern part of the Sierra del Negrete and the lower part of the Sot River with the Turia River, leaving the Chera-Sot de Chera Natural Park communicated and connected with the upper and lower Turia fluvial axis.
